Thanks for taking our questionnaire so quickly. As part of Acme's vendor assessment (SIG/CAIQ + SOC 2 cross-check), the security team has a follow-up on networking and isolation models for Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private. We need: 

- A concise network diagram for both Dedicated and Private (showing management plane, data plane, customer VPC boundaries, NAT/gateway points, and control-plane egress).
- A short explanation of how tenant isolation is enforced on Dedicated GPU pools (logical vs. physical isolation, VLANs, hypervisor assumptions).

- Any SOC 2 evidence pointers (control IDs or attachments) that map to these controls.

Can you share artifacts (diagram + evidence bundle) and a contact for technical validation? We have a deadline of 2026-03-10 for our procurement review.

Appreciate it — Andrea

Eve/Marissa — attaching first drafts. Notes below.

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood-dedicated-seg-diagram-v1.png (diagram, 1200x800)
- private-deployment-interfaces.pdf (sequence diagrams + IP/port table)

Summary of key points in the artifacts:
- Dedicated: dedicated GPU racks are assigned to a single customer at the physical host level when requested (reserved pools). We also support logical isolation via per-customer VLANs and strict iptables/host firewall rules at hypervisor level. Management plane (Redwood control plane) connects via a separate management network with egress allowed only to specific monitoring and SSO endpoints; customer data path never traverses this plane.
- Private (VPC): for Private deployments we provide two patterns — "Managed VPC Peering" (control plane peering) and "Private Control Plane" (customer hosts a thin control plane connector). Both patterns include a customer-side NAT/Gateway; we recommend using a dedicated subnetwork for model-serving traffic.
- Telemetry: recommended sources — VPC Flow Logs (Cloud provider native), Load Balancer access logs, Node host audit logs (journald/OS logs), application-level request traces (Corpora-trace headers), and KV-cache eviction metrics. Default retention: VPC Flow Logs 90 days, LB 30 days, host audit 180 days, application logs 30 days. We can extend per-customer on Dedicated for an add-on.
- SOC 2 pointers: network/perimeter controls map to CC6.1 (example) — see SOC2-2025-network-controls.pdf in our internal evidence bundle. I'll pull the exact control mapping into a single sheet next.

Flagging one open question: Marissa, can you confirm the exact retention for host audit logs in Dedicated (we currently roll to blob storage for 180 days by default)?

— Dev
